model_annotation: Figure 10 illustrates the effect of context masking on case tasks and adjectives, grouped by language family, with error bars indicating the standard deviation. The horizontal axis represents language family, labeled with categories including Indo-European, Uralic, Baltic, and Romance, listed in alphabetical order. The vertical axis represents error bars, labeled as “Error bars indicate the standard deviation,” with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 0.15, with tick marks at intervals of 0.05.  There are two sets of bars for each language family: one set labeled “TARG” in blue and one labeled “PERMUTE” in red. Within each language family, the “TARG” bar is positioned to the left of the “PERMUTE” bar. For the Indo-European family, the “TARG” bar reaches approximately 0.04, while the “PERMUTE” bar reaches approximately 0.08. In the Uralic family, both “TARG” and “PERMUTE” bars are around 0.12. The Baltic family shows a “TARG” bar at approximately 0.06 and a “PERMUTE” bar at approximately 0.13. Finally, the Romance family displays a “TARG” bar at approximately 0.08 and a “PERMUTE” bar at approximately 0.14. Error bars are present above each bar, indicating the standard deviation. No bars are visually emphasized through shading, bolding, outlining, or annotation.
